title.narrative: PERFORMANCE-BASED PARTNERSHIP SCHEME FOCUSING ON QUALITY PROGRAMMING, UNDERSTANDING CHANGE AND RESULTS FOR POOR HOUSEHOLDS AND COMMUNITIES

description.narrative: The Global Citizenship Education (GCE) programme aims to cultivate an informed and active Irish public that champions global responsibility. The combined effort of the programmes formal, non-formal and informal education empowers today’s Irish public while fostering a legacy of global leadership and responsibility for the next generation, building a foundation of enduring support for global and sustainable development and Ireland’s Official Development Assistance (ODA) programme. Almost 18,000 people have benefited from GOAL’s GCE programming in 2024. Through public events, campaigns and partnerships, almost 10,000 people in Ireland have engaged with GCE programming, facilitating them to become active global citizens, advocating for justice and sustainability in their communities. Over 4,000 primary students through GCE workshops and 3,500 young people through NextGen programming have been equipped with the knowledge, skills and global awareness to become the next generation of resilient changemakers of Ireland.. GOAL’s Global Youth Network (GYN) members act as advocates for ODA, SDGs and global justice and humanitarian issues through a Global Citizenship lens at local, regional, national and international platforms. GYN engage with an expanding circle of peers, networks and public audiences outside of, and additional to, the opportunities that GOAL provides, acting as amplifiers and multipliers of Global Citizenship messaging fostering support for ODA, SDGs and the global justice and humanitarian issues they seek to address.
